question: Into which two main parts is the Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) software partitioned?

options.a: Flight management and flight guidance applications
options.b: Aircraft interface/host platform and data link applications

justification: Page 5: The ATSU S/W is partitioned into two main parts: aircraft interface/host platform and data link applications.

question: Which service of the ATSU host platform software is used for the acquisition of aircraft parameters and system monitoring?
justification: Page 5: system management, used for the acquisition of the aircraft parameters for application S/W use and monitoring of the system: power supply and BITE functions.

question: In the ATSU modularity concept, what is the primary role of the 'Remote AOC' application?

options.a: Processing, printing, and display of received messages
options.b: Routing data to and from AOC peripherals
options.c: Generation and triggering of downlink messages

justification: Page 5: For the remote AOC applications, the ATSU only routes data to and from AOC peripherals.

question: Via which unit is the ATSU software uploaded into the system?
justification: Page 7: The ATSU S/W is uploaded via the Multipurpose Disk Drive Unit (MDDU).

question: During a complete ATSU S/W upload, why is a de-selection of the data loading required for each type of software?

options.a: To prevent the MDDU from overheating during long transfers
options.b: To ensure the ATSU can re-initialize until the DATALINK ATSU FAULT warning clears
options.c: To allow the FMGC to synchronize its database with the new ATSU software

justification: Page 7: If a complete S/W uploading is required, a de-selection of the ATSU data loading must be carried out, for each type of S/W, so that a re-initialization of the ATSU can be made until the DATALINK ATSU FAULT warning goes off on the EWD.

question: What indications are triggered on the flight deck when an Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) failure occurs?

options.a: Master Warning, continuous repetitive chime, and the SD status page
options.b: Master Caution, Single Chime, and DATALINK ATSU FAULT on the EWD
options.c: A red fault light on the overhead panel and an amber 'COMPANY STBY' memo

justification: Page 9: When there is an Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) failure, the message 'DATALINK ATSU FAULT' appears on the EWD, in this case, MASTER CAUTion light and Single Chime (SC) will be activated.

question: Where is the ATSU fault message displayed for the crew to identify inoperative systems?

options.a: In the INOP SYS column of the STATUS page
options.b: In the FAULT log of the MCDU COMM menu
options.c: On the Engine/Warning Display as a red prioritized warning

justification: Page 9: NOTE: In the INOP SYS column of the STATUS page, the ATSU fault message appears.

question: Which memo appears in green when the VHF Data Radio (VDR) 3, configured in VDL mode 2, is unavailable for data transmission?
justification: Page 9: When VHF Data Radio (VDR) 3, configured in VHF DataLink (VDL) mode 2, is not available for data transmission, the right memo 'VHF3 VOICE' appears in green.

question: How long does the 'HF VOICE' memo pulse in green when all installed HFDRs are in voice mode?
justification: Page 9: When all the HF Data Radio (HFDR) (if installed) are in voice mode, the right memo 'HF VOICE' pulses in green for 10 seconds and then stays stable.

question: During which flight phases are the DATALINK ATSU FAULT and COMPANY MSG warnings inhibited?
justification: Page 10: The Flight Phase Inhibition table shows phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 for DATALINK ATSU FAULT and the company memos.

question: What are the two primary functions provided by the ATIMS through the MCDU?

options.b: AOC hosted applications and air-ground communication management

justification: Page 11: The MCDU gives the following functions: Airline Operational Control (AOC) hosted applications and, air-ground communication management.

question: In the MCDU COMM MENU, what is the function of the 'AUDIT PRINT PAGE SET OFF' key?

options.a: It stops all data link printing functions across the aircraft
options.b: It disables the audit function directly without accessing the AUDIT page
options.c: It resets the printer after a communication failure

justification: Page 13: NOTE: The AUDIT PRINT PAGE SET OFF function is used to disable this function directly from this page without having to get access to the AUDIT page.

question: Under which conditions is the initialization through the COMM CONFIG menu considered complete?

options.a: When the ATSU is connected to the SITA network via SATCOM
options.b: When the ATSU receives a valid A/C registration, airline ID, and scan mask
options.c: When the GPS primary status is confirmed and the clock is synchronized

justification: Page 13: The initialization through COMM CONFIG menu is considered as completed when the Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) has received a valid aircraft registration number, airline identification and scan mask.

question: What information is displayed on the 'VHF3 DATA MODE' MCDU page?

options.a: The signal strength and frequency of the active VOR station
options.b: The selected regions, associated data link providers, and frequencies
options.c: The maintenance status of the three RMPs

justification: Page 13: The VHF3 DATA MODE page shows the various regions, which can be selected. Each region is associated with a data link service provider and a frequency.

question: Which MCDU menu allows a technician to print out exchanged messages per media and router for analysis?
justification: Page 15: AUDIT to print out exchanged messages per media and router depending on selection (found under MAINTENANCE STATUS).

question: Which essential parameter for ATSU router initialization is sent by the ATC Transponders?
justification: Page 19: Four essential parameters are required: A/C ICAO CODE (24bit address sent by the ATC Transponders)...

question: Which unit is responsible for sending the aircraft registration number to the ATSU during router initialization?
justification: Page 19: The A/C registration number is sent by the Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU).

question: What warning is displayed on the EWD if any of the four essential router initialization parameters are invalid?

options.b: DATALINK ATSU FAULT + ATSU INIT FAULT

justification: Page 19: Four essential parameters are required... Otherwise, the DATALINK ATSU FAULT+ ATSU INIT FAULT amber warnings are displayed on the Engine/Warning Display (EWD).

question: How does the ATSU create the Flight Identification parameter?

options.a: By reading the tail number from the CFDIU
options.b: By concatenating the airline ID and the flight number from the FMGC
options.c: By decoding the 24-bit ICAO address from the transponder

justification: Page 19: The ATSU creates the flight identification by concatenating the airline identification parameter and the flight number parameter coming from the Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC).

question: What is the purpose of the 'NEW SCAN SELECT' function in the VHF SCAN SELECT pages?

options.a: To initiate a manual scan for all available SITA stations
options.b: To erase the previous scan mask selection to allow a new configuration
options.c: To toggle between TLS and HAM test modes

justification: Page 21: The NEW SCAN SELECT function is used to erase the previous selection. The VHF3 SCAN MASK is compulsory for the router operation.

question: Which action must be performed after selecting service providers in the scan mask to finalize the router initialization?

options.a: Pressing the 'CONFIG ACTIVATE' LSK in the COMM CONFIG menu
options.b: Performing a hard reset of the ATSU via the C/B panel
options.c: Selecting 'REVERT AUTO' on the VHF3 DATA MODE page

justification: Page 23: To finalize the initialization the CONFIG ACTIVATE LSK in the COMM CONFIG menu must be pressed. When the initialization of the ATSU router is completed, the DATALINK ATSU FAULT + ATSU INIT FAULT warning goes off.

question: During an ATSU operational test in Voice mode, what indication on the Radio Management Panel (RMP) remains in the active window?
justification: Page 27: On the Radio Management Panel (RMP), the DATA indication stays in view in the active window. In this mode, communication tests with the ground can be done.

question: Which unit transmits UTC time and date to the ATSU as a backup to the aircraft clock?
justification: Page 35: As back-up of the clock, the MMR2 transmits the UTC time and date from a GPS source, on an ARINC 429 bus.

question: The ATSU sends 1 discrete signal to the 3 RMPs. What is the purpose of this signal?

options.a: To indicate which entity is controlling the VDR3
options.b: To synchronize the active frequency between RMPs
options.c: To initiate a self-test of the RMP communication buses

justification: Page 35: The ATSU sends 1 discrete signal to the 3 RMPs to indicate which entity is controlling the VDR3.

question: What is the primary purpose of the ATSU/FDIMU interface?

options.a: Loading of performance databases into the FMGC
options.b: Flight performance in uplink request and downlink AIDS reports
options.c: Recording of cockpit voice signals for the CVR

justification: Page 36: The ATSU/FDIMU interface is used for flight performance in uplink request and downlink AIDS reports.

question: Which system is optionally used to connect an Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) for the 'Less Paper in Cockpit' option?
justification: Page 36: NOTE: The AINS plugs are used to connect the Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) for customers who get the Less Paper in Cockpit (LCP) option.

question: If an aircraft loses communication with the GPS clock, how does the ATSU maintain valid UTC time for AOC messages?

options.a: It uses time signals from the FMGC 1
options.b: It acquires UTC data from the MMR2 on an ARINC 429 bus
options.c: It reverts to the local time entered manually on the COMM CONFIG page

justification: Page 35: The ATSU acquires Universal Time Coordinated (UTC) time and date from the clock... As back-up of the clock, the MMR2 transmits the UTC time and date from a GPS source.

question: How does the ATSU determine whether the aircraft is on ground or in flight for its logic functions?

options.a: Via a discrete input from the Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit (LGCIU)
options.b: By comparing Air Data/Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU) airspeed to 80 knots
options.c: Through ARINC 429 altitude data received from the Radio Altimeter

justification: Page 36: The ATSU receives, from the Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit (LGCIU), information on a discrete input to determine if the aircraft is on ground or in flight.

question: What is the primary use of the Mode S Data Link in the Elementary Surveillance (ELS) concept?

options.b: TCAS coordination, selective interrogation, and enhanced surveillance

justification: Page 38: Mode S: Data Link - Used for TCAS, selective interrogation, enhanced surveillance.

question: Which of the following is NOT an Elementary Surveillance (ELS) parameter sent to the ATC Center?
justification: Page 40: The Elementary Surveillance (ELS) sends to the ATC Center: aircraft identification, flight level. Roll angle is listed under specific parameters for enhanced surveillance (EHS).

question: What is the typical range limit for ADS-B broadcast signals using the transponder aerial?
justification: Page 42: Because ADS-B uses the transponder aerial, the range limit is 120NM.

question: How does Automatic Dependant Surveillance-Contract (ADS-C) differ from ADS-Broadcast (ADS-B)?

options.a: ADS-C is hosted by the transponder while ADS-B is hosted by the ATSU
options.b: ADS-C reports data requested in a contract between the airborne system and the ATC ground system
options.c: ADS-C requires no action from the flight crew while ADS-B requires manual triggering

justification: Page 42: The ADS-C application is hosted by the ATSU and reports data requested in a contract made between the airborne system and the ATC ground system.

question: What happens if an aircraft is flying outside of Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) coverage but has active ADS-C?

options.a: It can no longer be tracked by any ATC facility
options.b: It can still be tracked using worldwide data link range (SATCOM and HF)
options.c: The transponder automatically switches to 'Extended Squitters' to increase range

justification: Page 42: ADS-C uses the almost worldwide data link range and can track aircraft out of SSR coverage.

question: Which component of the Airbus Information Network System (AINS) provides server and data management functions on-board?
justification: Page 47: the Aircraft Network Server Unit (ANSU), which provides a powerful server and data management functions on-board the aircraft.

question: What is the primary function of the AINS Server Interface Unit (SIU)?

options.a: To host the electronic flight bag (EFB) software
options.b: To provide a security barrier between the avionics world and the open world
options.c: To manage wireless communications with the airport LAN

justification: Page 47: the Server Interface Unit (SIU), which protects the 'avionics world' systems from pollution or hacking intrusion from the 'open world', and gives a security barrier between the avionics and open networks.

question: The AINS Terminal Wireless LAN Unit (TWLU) is designed to operate under which condition?

options.a: During all flight phases above 10,000 feet
options.b: Only when the aircraft is on the ground
options.c: Only during approach and landing phases

justification: Page 53: The function of the TWLU is to operate only while the aircraft is on the ground.

question: How are the SIU, ANSU, and TWLU supplied with power?

options.b: 115V AC from BUS 2 via a circuit breaker

justification: Page 55: The SIU, the ANSU and the TWLU are supplied with 115V AC from the 115V AC BUS 2 bar 218XP-B via a Circuit Breaker (C/B).

question: If the Server Interface Unit (SIU) is removed for maintenance, what happens to the cockpit peripheral connections?

options.a: They automatically switch to the standby FMGC
options.b: MCDU 3 and the printer connections with the CFDIU are lost
options.c: Only the laptop EFB connection is affected; the printer remains functional

justification: Page 57: NOTE: If the SIU is removed (e.g for maintenance purpose), the MCDU 3 and the printer connections with the CFDIU are lost as they are switched internally in the SIU.

question: After an AINS software reset using the switch on the 48VU panel, how long must the crew wait before using the AINS and CINS?
justification: Page 57: After the software reset, it is necessary to wait approximately 15 minutes before using the AINS and the CINS.

question: Which VHF Data Radio (VDR) is typically reserved for ATSU functions and backup voice communications?
justification: Page 61: VDR 3 is used for Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) functions and as back-up voice communications if there is a failure of system 1 or 2.

question: What is the standard frequency range for the aircraft's VHF system?
justification: Page 89: The VHF system operates within the frequency range of 118.00 to 136.975 MHz.

question: On the Radio Management Panel (RMP), what happens to the previous active frequency when a new standby frequency is transferred?

options.a: It is permanently deleted from the RMP memory
options.b: It becomes the new standby frequency
options.c: It is stored in the FMGC navigation database

justification: Page 96: Pressing the transfer pushbutton, activates the frequency and displays it in the active window, whereas the previous active frequency becomes stand-by.

question: How does an operator select multiple radio receivers for simultaneous listening on the Audio Control Panel (ACP)?

options.a: By pulling the corresponding reception knobs out
options.b: By pressing and releasing the reception knobs so they come on white
options.c: By using the 'ALL' button on the RMP

justification: Page 96: To select a receiver, the related reception knob must be released out. The reception knob comes on white... several reception knobs can be selected simultaneously.

question: If RMP 1 fails, how can the VHF 1 transceiver still be controlled?

options.a: It can only be controlled by the FMGC through automatic tuning
options.b: It can be controlled by another RMP through Serial input port B
options.c: It is permanently lost until the RMP is replaced

justification: Page 88: The VHF transceiver has 2 serial input ports : Serial input port A for normal use and serial input port B in case of RMP failure.

question: What is the ECAM indication if a VHF system emits continuously for more than one minute?
justification: Page 88: In case of continuous emitting, the ECAM displays: - COM: VHF 1/2 EMITTING.

question: Where is the HF antenna located on the Airbus Single Aisle aircraft?

options.a: On the top of the fuselage behind the cockpit
options.b: Behind the leading edge of the vertical stabilizer

justification: Page 67: The HF antenna is installed behind the leading edge of the vertical stabilizer.

question: What is the frequency range for the HF communication system?
justification: Page 85: The HF system operates within the frequency range of 2.8 to 23.999 MHz.

question: Which unit controls the tuning operations for the HF transceivers via ARINC 429 numeric messages?
justification: Page 86: The Radio Management Panel (RMP) controls the tuning operations which are transmitted to the transceiver (XCVR) by a numeric message in compliance with ARINC 429.

question: If an aircraft is being jacked for maintenance with weight off wheels, how is the HF BITE affected?

options.a: The HF system automatically enters a full power test mode
options.b: The LGCIU signal allows the HF BITE to accurately count flight legs
options.c: The HF BITE assumes the aircraft is in flight based on the LGCIU status

justification: Page 86: The Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit (LGCIU) indicates the flight or ground status... used by the HF BITE, in order to count the flight legs.

question: Where is the SELCAL code panel located on the aircraft?
justification: Page 69: The SELCAL panel, AMU, HF and VHF Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) are in the aft avionics compartment. Page 91 also specifies 80VU.

question: How is a crew member alerted on the ACP when a valid SELCAL code is received?

options.a: A green 'DATA' light appears on the RMP
options.b: The CALL light flashes amber on the corresponding communication channel
options.c: A continuous buzzer sounds from the area microphone

justification: Page 90: On the ACPs, the CALL light, corresponding to the communication channel used, flashes amber.

question: Which of the following methods can be used to cancel a SELCAL call alert?

options.a: Pressing the RESET key on any ACP or activating the PTT on the called channel
options.b: Rotating the volume control knob on the AMU
options.c: Switching off the RMP for 5 seconds

justification: Page 90: The call is cancelled using the RESET key on one ACP, or selecting the called channel and activating the Push To Talk (PTT).

question: Which interphone system is intended for ground use only by maintenance technicians?
justification: Page 63: Service interphone (on ground only) for maintenance technician communication with cockpit or cabin.

question: How many service interphone jacks are installed around the aircraft?
justification: Page 224: The SVCE INTPH SYS is made of: - eight interphone jacks.

question: What is the function of the five isolation units in the service interphone system?

options.a: To amplify audio signals for long wire runs
options.b: To minimize effects of a short-circuit in a maintenance jack-socket
options.c: To separate flight crew communications from ground crew audio

justification: Page 224: five isolation units, If there is a short-circuit condition in a maintenance-interphone jack-socket, the isolation unit will keep the effects of the failure on the service interphone system to a minimum.

question: On the Audio Control Panel, what does the illumination of the green bars on the INT transmission key indicate?

options.a: A call is being received from the purser
options.b: The flight interphone is ready to operate

justification: Page 94: Selection of the INT transmission key lights the green bars, indicating that the flight interphone is ready to operate.

question: What happens to the flight interphone communication if a radio emission is keyed while the INT/RAD switch is in the INT position?

options.a: The radio emission is blocked until the interphone is released
options.b: Both signals are mixed and transmitted simultaneously
options.c: The flight interphone is momentarily cut

justification: Page 94: NOTE: The radio function has priority over the flight interphone function. So, even with the INT/RAD switch in INT position, the flight interphone is momentarily cut during a radio emission.

question: Why is the service interphone system automatically disabled when the aircraft is jacked with weight off wheels?

options.a: To save battery power for emergency systems
options.b: To stop potential static noise from wires acting as antennae
options.c: To prevent accidental triggering of the landing gear retraction

justification: Page 336: With weight off wheels, the service interphone system is disabled... The reason for this is to stop potential static noise started and amplified through the AMU due to the length of wires acting as antennae.

question: If the LGCIU signal is unavailable on the ground, how can maintenance personnel establish service interphone communication?

options.a: By pulling and resetting the CIDS director circuit breakers
options.b: By switching the SVCE INT OVRD P/BSW to 'ON' on the 50VU panel
options.c: By selecting 'STBY' on all RMPs simultaneously

justification: Page 336: To re-enable the service interphone, the SerViCE INTerphone OVeRriDe P/BSW must be switched to 'ON'. The Service Interphone Override switch is on the Maintenance Panel 50VU.

question: Which unit is responsible for assigning priorities to various PA sources and transmitting digital signals to the DEU As?
justification: Page 213: The Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) directors (DIRs) accept audio signals from the various Passenger Address (PA) sources... The active DIR assigns priorities to each source. It transmits the signal in digital form via the two top-line data buses to the type A Decoder/Encoder Units (DEUs).

question: What is the standard first priority for Passenger Address announcements?
justification: Page 213: The basic levels of priority are the following ones: - 1st priority: Flight compartment.

question: By how many decibels is the PA volume automatically increased when an engine is running?
justification: Page 214: When an engine is running, the PA volume is increased automatically by + 6 dB.

question: Which system component monitors for rapid decompression to trigger an automatic PA announcement increase of +4 dB?
justification: Page 214: When an engine is running, the PA volume is increased automatically by + 6 dB, and by + 4 dB in the event of cabin depressurization, monitored by the Cabin Pressure Controller (CPC).

question: How is acoustic feedback avoided if the cockpit door is opened during a PA announcement?

options.a: The cockpit loudspeaker is completely muted
options.b: The PA volume decreases in the cockpit door area
options.c: The PA system is automatically disconnected until the door is closed

justification: Page 214: If during a PA announcement the cockpit door is opened, there is a volume decrease of the PA announcement in the cockpit door area, to avoid a feedback with the cockpit.

question: What type of data is exchanged between the Audio Management Unit (AMU) and the Audio Control Panels (ACPs)?
justification: Page 80: ACP-AMU link is done by ARINC 429 buses. Only digital data are exchanged between the AMU and the ACPs. There are no audio signals inside the ACPs.

question: Where is the actual volume control processing for radio and interphone achieved?
justification: Page 80: The volume control function is achieved by digital transmission of the knobs position to the AMU. Volume control is achieved inside the AMU.

question: What is the effect of the AMU muting circuit when a transmission is keyed by a push-to-talk switch?

options.a: It disconnects all headsets to prevent listener fatigue
options.b: It decreases the gain and band-pass of the loudspeaker amplifiers
options.c: It sends a ground signal to the FWC to suppress Master Warning audio

justification: Page 82: When a transmission is keyed by any push to talk switch, a ground signal is delivered to the two loudspeaker amplifiers. This ground signal decreases the gain and band-pass of the loudspeaker amplifiers.

question: On how many independent channels does the CVR record audio signals?
justification: Page 109: In normal mode, the CVR records, on four independent channels, the audio signals...

question: What audio is recorded on CVR Channel 4?

options.b: Ambient noise picked up by the area microphone
options.c: Datalink message archives from the ATSU

justification: Page 109: Channel 4 records the ambient noise picked up by the area microphone and supplied through a pre-amplifier to the CVR.

question: What specific ground conditions must be met for the CVR erase function to operate?

options.a: Aircraft on ground, engines running, and parking brake off
options.b: Aircraft on ground, landing gear shock absorbers compressed, and parking brake applied
options.c: Aircraft on ground, weight-on-wheels signal present, and slats/flaps extended

justification: Page 109: Erase is only possible, aircraft on the ground, R and L main landing gear shock absorbers compressed and parking brake applied.

question: If the engines are shut down, how must the CVR be energized for testing?

options.a: By selecting 'CVR TEST' on the MCDU maintenance menu
options.b: By pressing the GND CTL P/B on the RCDR panel
options.c: By initiating an APU start sequence

justification: Page 109: NOTE: If the engines are shut down, the CVR must first be energized by pressing the GND CTL P/B on the RCDR panel.

question: How long does the CVR continue to run after the second engine shutdown on the ground?
justification: Page 109: The CVR is automatically supplied... on the ground until a maximum of five minutes after the second engine shutdown.

question: In CVR 'CAA mode', when are the hand microphones considered 'HOT'?

options.a: At all times for voice/noise pick-up
options.b: Only when the oxygen mask pressure switch is closed
options.c: Only when the Push-To-Talk (PTT) switch on the microphone is activated

justification: Page 112: In CAA mode... The hand microphones are only 'HOT' when the Push-To-Talk (PTT) switch on the microphone is activated.

question: What is the result of selecting the 'CAPT 3' position on the AUDIO SWITCHING selector?

options.a: The Captain uses the F/O's Audio Control Panel
options.b: The Captain uses the 3rd occupant ACP, and 3rd occupant audio equipment is disabled
options.c: The Captain's audio is recorded directly to the ATSU as well as the CVR

justification: Page 78: CAPT 3 POSITION: In this position, the CAPT will use the 3rd occupant ACP. The 3rd occupant audio equipment cannot be used.

question: What happens in the CIDS system if the Service Bus power is lost?

options.a: The system shuts down completely to preserve the ESS BUS
options.b: The second DIR, non-essential DEU circuits, and the FAP become inoperative
options.c: The system switches all loads to the HOT BAT BUS for 30 minutes

justification: Page 159: If SVCE BUS power is unavailable, the following items of equipment are inoperative: - the second DIR, - the non essential DEU circuits, - the FAP.

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: Which function of the ADIRU uses laser gyros and accelerometers to provide attitude and heading data?
justification: Page 342: Each ADIRU combines... an Air Data Reference (ADR) unit, a strapdown Inertial Reference (IR) unit, using laser gyros and accelerometers.

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: Where are the three ADIRUs located in the aircraft?

options.c: On the center pedestal beneath the MCDUs

justification: Page 436: The 3 ADIRUs are in the aft avionics compartment forward of the 80VU.

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: Which unit is responsible for converting pitot and static pressure into digital ARINC 429 format for the ADIRU?
justification: Page 438: Three Pitot probes provide total pressure to three Air Data Modules (ADMs), which convert this pressure into digital format: ARINC 429.

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: During ADIRU alignment through the MCDU, what must be the position of the MSU selector switches?
justification: Page 448: To perform the three IRs alignments, the three OFF/NAVigation/ATTitude selector switches on the Air Data/Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) Mode Selector Unit (MSU) must be set to NAV position.

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: If both FMGCs have failed, how can the crew tune the navigation receivers?

options.a: By using the ADIRS Mode Selector Unit in ATT mode
options.b: By using the backup tuning mode on RMP 1 and 2
options.c: By manually entering frequencies on the ISIS indicator

justification: Page 370: Radio Management Panel (RMP) 1 and 2 are capable of tuning the own side Navigation receivers in backup mode if both FMGCs have failed...

subtopic: Air Data and Inertial Reference System (ADIRS)
question: What indication appears on the upper ECAM display unit at the end of a successful IR alignment process?

options.b: The IRS IN ALIGN 1 MN indication goes out of view

justification: Page 448: On the upper ECAM display unit, the IRS IN ALIGN 1 MN indication goes out of view at the end of the alignment process.

question: Which conventional instruments does the Integrated Standby Instrument System (ISIS) replace?

options.b: Standby altimeter, horizon indicator, and AirSpeed Indicator (ASI)

justification: Page 450: The Integrated Standby Instrument System (ISIS) is a combined standby altimeter, horizon indicator and AirSpeed Indicator (ASI).

question: How long is the initialization display shown when the ISIS is first energized?
justification: Page 450: As soon as the ISIS is energized, it shows the initialization display for 90 s.

question: What is indicated by the trapezoidal index beneath the roll indicator on the ISIS standby horizon?
justification: Page 458: A trapezoidal index, which can move beneath the roll indicator, represents the A/C lateral acceleration (sideslip).

question: Which button on the ISIS is used to program characteristic speeds and altitudes on the display scales?
justification: Page 460: Pushing the BUGS P/B shows the BUGS display. This display is used to program characteristic speeds and altitudes displayed on the related speed and altitude scales.

question: Under what condition is the ISIS functional test inhibited?

options.a: Whenever the aircraft is on the ground
options.b: When the Calibrated Air Speed (CAS) is greater than 60 knots
options.c: When the Landing System (LS) mode is active

justification: Page 462: NOTE: The ISIS has an internal flight/ground logic... The test is inhibited when the Calibrated Air Speed (CAS) is greater than 60 kts.

question: What is the backup power supply for the ISIS if the DC Essential Bus is not available?
justification: Page 464: If DC ESS BUS is not available, a back-up of 28V DC is automatically supplied from the HOT BATtery BUS if airspeed is greater than 50 kts.

question: Which two navigation functions are combined into a single Multi-Mode Receiver (MMR) unit?
justification: Page 472: The Multi-Mode Receiver (MMR) system is a navigation sensor with 3 internal receivers: MMR = ILS + GPS.

question: Where are the ILS Localizer and Glide Slope antennas typically installed?
justification: Page 480: The Multi-mode Receiver antennas are installed... in the radome for the G/S and LOC dual antennas.

question: In the GPS system architecture, how many satellites are necessary for the receiver to compute the aircraft position?
justification: Page 478: The principle of GPS position computation is based on the measurement of transmission time of the GPS signals broadcast by at least four satellites.

question: What does the 'GPS PRIMARY' message on the Navigation Display (ND) indicate?

options.a: The GPS is the only available navigation source
options.b: The GPS is receiving adequate signals to calculate a present position
options.c: The FMGC has selected GPS 1 as the master source

justification: Page 380: GPS when receiving adequate signals to calculate a present position will be annotated at the bottom of the ND. This is displayed as 'GPS PRIMARY'.

question: To preserve side segregation, which input port of ADIRU 3 should be selected if ADIRU 1 fails in a dual GPS architecture?
justification: Page 486: In case of one ADIRU 1 failure, the FMGC 1 uses ADIRU 3/GPS 1 data. (Preserving segregation: GPS 1/ADIRU 1/FMGC 1 and GPS 2/ADIRU 2/FMGC 2).

question: What logic inhibits frequency changes in the MMR unit during an ILS approach?

options.a: The LGCIU when landing gear is extended
options.b: The FMGC when LAND mode is armed below 700 feet
options.c: The EGPWC when a terrain caution is detected

justification: Page 489: NOTE: A discrete signal sent by the FMGC inhibits any frequency change in the MMR unit when LAND mode is armed below 700 ft.

question: What is the maximum range for rain detection using the Weather Radar (WXR) system?
justification: Page 492: Maximum range: For rain detection: 320 NM.

question: In which EFIS mode is the WXR image NOT displayed?
justification: Page 497: Radar image... are displayed in all EFIS modes (ARC and ROSE) but not in PLAN mode.

question: What safety precaution must be observed for personnel when the WXR is 'ON' on the ground?

options.a: Personnel should not be within 1.5 meters of the antenna
options.b: Personnel should not be within 5 meters of the radome
options.c: Personnel should not be within 60 meters of the aircraft nose

justification: Page 412: WARNING: when the WXR is 'ON': - personnel should not be within 5 meters of the radome.

question: What is the purpose of the 'multiscan' function in the Weather Radar system?

options.a: To scan both horizontal and vertical planes simultaneously
options.b: To provide significant weather display at all ranges essentially clutter-free
options.c: To track terrain elevation using the GPS database

justification: Page 412: The multiscan is a radar function that displays all significant weather at all ranges... on a display that is essentially clutter-free.

question: How does the WXR system determine the optimum tilt angle when the MULTISCAN SW is set to AUTO?

options.a: By using pitch data from the ADIRU only
options.b: By using terrain altitude information from the EGPWS
options.c: By scanning the horizon and calculating the strongest reflection

justification: Page 412: The autotilt function uses the terrain altitude information of the EGPWS. Based on the aircraft altitude above the terrain... the EGPWS determines the optimum tilt angle.

question: What is the result on the WXR/PWS transceiver if both EFIS control panels are set to PLAN mode?

options.a: The transceiver remains in standby mode
options.c: The transceiver continues scanning but display is inhibited

justification: Page 503: NOTE: When both EFIS control panels are in PLAN mode, the WXR/PWS transceiver is de-energized.

question: Up to what altitude is the radio height data displayed on the PFD?
justification: Page 408: RA data is supplied to several users and is displayed on both PFDs at all times below 2500 feet Above Ground Level (AGL).

question: What is the operating frequency range of the Radio Altimeter (RA) transceiver?
justification: Page 518: The RA transceiver measures the radio height... The transceiver operates in a frequency range of 4.200 to 4.400 MHz.

question: What happens if RA 1 transceiver fails during normal flight below 2,500 feet?

options.a: The CAPT PFD display for radio height is permanently lost
options.b: The DMC automatically switches the display to RA 2 data
options.c: The ADIRU 1 provides a computed barometric altitude instead

justification: Page 518: In normal operation, RA 1 provides the radio height to the CAPT PFD... In case of one transceiver failure the DMC automatically switches to the other one.

question: What is the function of the Resolution Advisory (RA) volume in the TCAS system?

options.a: It identifies traffic that does not represent a collision threat
options.b: It triggers an aural and visual alarm for intruders representing a collision threat
options.c: It provides a 120 NM search area around the aircraft

justification: Page 520: RA VOLUME: When the intruder represents a collision threat, the TCAS (or T2CAS) triggers an aural and visual alarm known as Resolution Advisory (RA).

question: How many TCAS antennas are installed on the aircraft?
justification: Page 531: The Traffic alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) includes: ... - 2 antennas (1 top and 1 bottom).

question: What is the primary role of the 'Suppressor' coaxial in the TCAS system?

options.a: To amplify signals between the top and bottom antennas
options.b: To inhibit other systems in the same frequency range and prevent simultaneous transmission
options.c: To filter out background noise from ground-based radar

justification: Page 531: A suppressor signal is transmitted, via a coaxial... to inhibit the other systems and to prevent simultaneous transmission.

question: In case of a TCAS warning, which systems have a higher priority and will inhibit TCAS aural alerts?

options.c: GPS primary lost and ADIRU alignment messages

justification: Page 532: Various discrete signals are used for inhibition by equipment with higher priority than the TCAS... These priorities are: - Stall, - WindShear, - Predictive WindShear (PWS), - Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System (EGPWS) messages.

question: Which TCAS mode is automatically selected by the system when on the ground to reduce nuisance alerts?
justification: Page 532: Operating mode: ... - ground display mode (TA mode).

question: What are the two 'ENHANCED' functions added to the basic GPWS modes in an EGPWS system?

options.b: Terrain Clearance Floor (TCF) and Terrain Awareness alerting and Display (TAD)
options.c: GPS position fixing and SATCOM data link

justification: Page 534: The 'ENHANCED' functions added to the basic GPWS modes are: -Terrain Clearance Floor (TCF)... - Terrain Awareness alerting and Display (TAD).

question: What is the effect of pressing the 'SYS' P/BSW on the GPWS control panel to the 'OFF' position?

options.a: It inhibits only the Terrain Awareness Display (TAD)
options.b: It inhibits all GPWS warnings (modes 1 to 5)
options.c: It resets the EGPWC for a standard power-up test

justification: Page 540: the SYStem P/BSW with the white OFF legend, inhibits all the GPWS warnings (mode 1 to 5).

question: What specific visual indication on the ND is provided by the T2CAS system if the aircraft cannot climb over terrain with a sufficient safety margin?

options.a: A solid red background with the word 'PULL UP'
options.b: Visual black crosses displayed in the solid red area

justification: Page 543: If GCAM predicts that the A/C can not climb over the terrain with sufficient safety margin... visual black crosses are displayed in the solid red on the ND.

question: Which navigation source does the EGPWC use as its highest priority for aircraft position?
justification: Page 540: The EGPWC uses preferably GPS position, then IRS latitude and longitude data...

question: Does the Automatic Flight System (AFS) move the side sticks or thrust levers during operation?

options.a: Yes, they move to provide tactile feedback to the pilot
options.b: No, they do not move automatically during AFS operation
options.c: Only the thrust levers move during autothrust operation

justification: Page 614: NOTE: During AFS operation, side sticks and thrust levers do not move automatically.

question: What are the two distinct parts that make up each Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC)?

options.b: Flight Management (FM) and Flight Guidance (FG) parts

justification: Page 616: Each FMGC is made of two parts: the Flight Management (FM) part and the Flight Guidance (FG) part.

question: In FMGC 'Single Mode', how are the MCDUs driven?

options.a: Each MCDU is driven by its ownside FM part
options.b: Both MCDUs are driven by the remaining healthy FM part
options.c: The MCDUs are disabled and backup nav must be used

justification: Page 701: SINGLE MODE: If one FM part has failed, a single mode is active. Both MCDUs are driven by the remaining FM part.

question: How often does the navigation database in the FMGC require updating?
justification: Page 704: This database has a tailored coverage, updated every 28 days.

question: What triggers the FMGC system to revert from Normal to Independent mode?

options.a: A failure of the ADIRU 1 airspeed signal
options.b: A disagreement between the two FM parts
options.c: Manual selection of the backup nav on the MCDU MENU

justification: Page 701: INDEPENDENT MODE: If the FM parts disagree... the system then reverts to independent mode.

question: Under what condition is the 'FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF' message displayed on the MCDUs?

options.a: When aircraft position difference between FMGCs is greater than 1 Nm
options.b: When aircraft position difference between FMGCs is greater than 5 Nm
options.c: When the GPS primary status is lost on both sides

justification: Page 701: If the difference is greater than 5 Nm, 2 tons or 2 Kts respectively, an appropriate message is displayed on the MCDUs: - FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF...

question: Which unit calculates the orders for the autothrust function (A/THR)?
justification: Page 635: To get the A/THR function, the thrust target computed by the Flight Management and Guidance Computers (FMGCs) is chosen by the Flight Control Unit (FCU).

question: What is indicated by the green message 'A. FLOOR' with an amber flashing box on the Flight Mode Annunciator (FMA)?

options.a: The autothrust has failed and must be reset
options.b: The system has detected an excessive Angle-Of-Attack and is ordering maximum thrust
options.c: The aircraft is below 100 feet RA during landing

justification: Page 675: In case of excessive AOA or avoidance maneuver... the engine thrust becomes equal to the TOGA thrust... the green message A. FLOOR with an amber flashing box is displayed on the FMA.

question: When is the RETARD mode for autothrust available?

options.a: During takeoff run to prevent engine overspeed
options.b: Only in automatic landing below 40 feet RA for the flare phase
options.c: During emergency descent when VMO is exceeded

justification: Page 675: Beside these two modes, RETARD is only available in automatic landing when engine thrust has to be reduced to idle for the flare phase below 40 feet RA.

question: What is the consequence of autothrust (A/THR) disconnection when the thrust lever is within a detent?

options.a: Thrust immediately reverts to the physical lever position
options.b: Thrust on the corresponding engine is frozen at its last value (memo mode)
options.c: The engines automatically shut down for safety

justification: Page 676: after FCU P/BSW disconnection, or failure: - when a thrust lever is in its detent, the thrust on the corresponding engine is frozen at its last value just before the disconnection (memo mode).

question: In the event of one engine failure, what is the new active zone for A/THR activation on the thrust levers?

options.a: Between the CL detent and the 0 stop
options.b: Between the FLX/MCT detent and the 0 stop
options.c: Between the TOGA stop and the CL detent

justification: Page 672: NOTE: In case of one engine failure, the A/THR activation zone is between the FLX/MCT detent and the 0 stop, instead of the CL detent, and the 0 stop.

question: Which unit is responsible for the 'Rudder Travel Limitation' function?
justification: Page 620: The basic functions of the Flight Augmentation Computer (FAC) are: ... - rudder travel limitation.

question: Where is the Fault Isolation and Detection System (FIDS) function active?
justification: Page 621: The FIDS function is only active in FAC 1.

question: What parameters are used by the FAC to compute the aircraft weight in flight?

options.a: Fuel quantity and center of gravity data from FQIC
options.b: ADIRS, FMGC, and Slat Flap Control Computer (SFCC) parameters
options.c: Radio Alt and Glide Slope deviation signals

justification: Page 659: In flight, the FAC computes the weight with the Air Data/Inertial Reference System (ADIRS), FMGC and Slat Flap Control Computer (SFCC) parameters.

question: How many functions does the FAC yaw damper have?
justification: Page 620: The yaw damper has four functions and controls the rudder via yaw damper actuators.

question: What is the consequence of a failure of the two ADIRUs on the flight envelope protection?

options.a: The system switches to standby GPS altitude
options.b: The alpha-floor detection does not operate
options.c: The yaw damper reverts to mechanical linkage only

justification: Page 661: If there is a failure of the two ADIRS, the alpha-floor detection does not operate.

question: On ground, how is a FAC reset attempted if a computer fault light appears on the ECAM?

options.a: The reset is automatic when the fault disappears, with engines shut down
options.b: The pilot must press the instinctive disconnect on the side stick
options.c: The C/B must be pulled for exactly 7 minutes

justification: Page 654: NOTE: On ground with engines shut down, the reset is automatic when the fault disappears.

question: What happens to the FCU display windows if both processing channels (FCU 1 and FCU 2) fail?

options.a: They display the last valid data from the FMGC
options.b: All FCU controls are inoperative and AP/FD functions are unavailable
options.c: They switch to a simplified backup battery-powered mode

justification: Page 689: If both channels fail, all FCU controls are inoperative: A/THR, AP/Flight Director (FD) 1 and AP/FD 2 are not available.

question: In the FCU Vertical Speed (V/S) control knob operation, what does 'pushing' the knob command?

options.b: An immediate level off with a zero target
options.c: Selection of the managed flight path angle mode

justification: Page 697: Pushing the V/S FPA rotary knob will command an immediate level off by engaging the V/S FPA mode with a zero target as displayed in the FCU window.

question: Which condition is necessary to engage the Autopilot (AP) for maintenance purposes on the ground with engines shut down?

options.a: Both FMGCs must be in Independent mode
options.c: External 115V AC power must be disconnected

justification: Page 628: For maintenance purposes, the AP can be engaged on ground with both engines shut down. Hydraulic power is not required.

question: What is the minimum time an aircraft must be airborne before the Autopilot can be engaged in flight?
justification: Page 628: The AP can be engaged in flight, provided the aircraft has been airborne for at least 5 seconds.

question: In cruise, what happens if the pilot attempts to engage a second Autopilot (AP) while one is already active?

options.b: The second AP engagement is inhibited
options.c: Engaging the second AP disengages the first one

justification: Page 628: In cruise, only one AP can be engaged at a time... Engaging the second AP disengages the first one.

question: What occurs automatically to the Autopilot when one engine is started on the ground?

options.a: The AP engages in takeoff mode
options.c: The AP switches to internal battery power

justification: Page 628: When an engine is started, the AP disengages.

question: What causes the Autopilot to disengage if the pilot applies manual pressure to the flight controls?

options.a: Any movement of the side stick beyond the neutral dead-zone
options.b: If a pedal or side stick load threshold is overridden
options.c: A failure signal from the ELAC due to surface disagreement

justification: Page 628: When the AP is engaged, the load thresholds on the rudder pedals and the side sticks are increased. If a pedal or side stick load threshold is overridden, the AP disengages.

question: During the landing rollout at low speed (approx. 60 knots), what is the normal procedure for disengaging the Autopilot?

options.b: Pressing a takeover pushbutton on the side stick
options.c: Selecting 'OFF' on the ADIRS Mode Selector Unit

justification: Page 629: During roll out, at low speed (about 60 knots), the pilot normally disengages the AP by pressing a takeover pushbutton located on the side stick.

question: During landing rollout with the AP engaged, to what position is the Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer (THS) reset?
justification: Page 629: During roll out... The THS is reset to 0.5 nose up.

question: How is the engagement of Flight Director 1 (FD1) and FD2 indicated on the PFD?

options.a: A green 'FD' text in the center of the display
options.b: A '1FD2' indication on the top right of the PFD
options.c: Three green bars on the MCDU status page

justification: Page 631: 1FD2 indication is displayed on each PFD to show that FD1 is engaged on the CAPT side and FD2 is engaged on the F/O side.

question: What happens to the Flight Director (FD) symbols on the PFD if the HDG-V/S / TRK-FPA P/BSW on the FCU is pressed?

options.a: The FD bars are removed and replaced by FPD/FPV symbols
options.b: The FD bars flash for 10 seconds to indicate a mode change
options.c: The FD bars turn red to indicate an invalid guidance mode

justification: Page 631: There are two types of symbols: the FD bars, the Flight Path Director (FPD) and Flight Path Vector (FPV) symbols. The central ... P/BSW on the FCU makes the pilots switch between these two types of symbols.

question: Under what condition will the Flight Director bars flash on the PFD for 10 seconds?

options.c: When the aircraft enters the EGPWS warning envelope

justification: Page 633: NOTE: At certain system configuration changes, the FMGCs send a command to the DMCs to make the FD bars flash for 10 seconds.

question: What does the 'LAND TEST' on the MCDU provide to maintenance personnel?

options.a: A simulated landing to check landing gear vibration
options.b: The test availability of the LANDing mode and equipment for Category 3
options.c: A printout of the last 10 successful autolandings

justification: Page 640: The LAND TEST gives the test availability of the LANDing mode and equipment required to obtain CATegory 3.

question: When LAND mode is engaged and the autopilot is active, how is yaw damping controlled?

options.a: Directly by the FMGC yaw guidance order
options.b: By the FAC using the Dutch roll damping law
options.c: By the ELAC using the normal yaw axis law

justification: Page 652: With the autopilot engaged and the Land Mode activated, Dutch roll damping and Turn coordination are inhibited and yaw damping is accomplished directly from the FMGC yaw guidance order.

question: At what altitude during an automatic landing does the 'RETARD' auto call out trigger?
justification: Page 675: RETARD is only available in automatic landing when engine thrust has to be reduced to idle for the flare phase below 40 feet RA.

question: Which action automatically engages the Autothrust (A/THR) function during a Go-Around?

options.a: Pressing the APPR button on the FCU
options.b: Setting the thrust levers to the TOGA stop

justification: Page 635: The A/THR is engaged automatically: - when the AP/Flight Director (FD) is engaged in Take-Off (TO) or Go Around (GA) modes. (Initiated by levers to TOGA).

question: If an aircraft is in Go-Around mode, which computer provides the engine failure compensation fast law for the yaw damper?
justification: Page 644: engine failure compensation fast law is given by the FAC using the ADIRS data in Take-Off/Go-Around (TOGA) or RunWaY modes only.

question: What is the active/standby relationship of the two identical processing channels (FCU 1 and 2) inside the single FCU panel?

options.a: They operate in active/active parallel mode
options.b: Only one channel is active at a time, the other is in standby
options.c: FCU 1 controls the Captain's PFD while FCU 2 controls the F/O's

justification: Page 689: Only one channel is active at a time, the other is in standby.

question: In a dual autopilot approach (AP1+2), which autopilot has priority if both are engaged?

options.b: AP1 has priority, AP2 is in standby
options.c: They share priority through the cross-talk bus

justification: Page 683: AP1 has priority, AP2 is in standby. The FCCs use the AP1 commands first.

question: If an FCU processor failure occurs, how can the remaining healthy channel be identified by the crew?

options.a: By a red 'FCU FAIL' message on the EWD
options.b: Automatic switching occurs; the failure is transparent if only one channel fails
options.c: The display windows on the failed side will go blank

justification: Page 689: This description implies manual intervention is only needed if BOTH channels fail. Note states: 'Only one channel is active at a time... if both channels fail, all FCU controls are inoperative'.

question: What does a non-lit Flight Director (FD) pushbutton on the FCU signify?

options.a: The FD is in managed mode
options.b: No FD symbols can be displayed on the corresponding PFD

justification: Page 631: A non lit FD P/BSW means that no FD symbols can be displayed on the corresponding PFD.

question: Below 400 feet during a LAND mode approach, how can the mode be disengaged?

options.a: By pressing the APPR button on the FCU
options.c: By retarding the thrust levers to idle

justification: Page 699: NOTE: Below 400 ft, LAND mode can only be disengaged by activating GO-AROUND.

question: What is the primary role of the Flight Management (FM) part of the FMGC?

options.b: Flight plan definition, revision, and monitoring

justification: Page 616: The FM part gives the functions related to flight plan definition, revision and monitoring.

question: Which database contains the optimal speed schedules and profiles used by the FM function?
justification: Page 705: The performance database contains optimal speed schedules for the expected range of operating conditions.

question: In FMGC 'Single Mode' due to an FM part failure, what message appears on the MCDU corresponding to the failed side?
justification: Page 701: SINGLE MODE: If one FM part has failed... A white message OPP FMGC IN PROGRESS is displayed on the MCDU corresponding to the failed FMGC.

question: When the Autopilot (AP) is engaged, what happens to the tactile feel of the rudder pedals and side sticks?

options.a: The load thresholds are decreased for easier override
options.c: They are mechanically locked and cannot be moved

justification: Page 628: When the AP is engaged, the load thresholds on the rudder pedals and the side sticks are increased.

question: During takeoff, below 30 feet RA when a Localizer (LOC) signal is available, which symbol replaces the roll bar on the PFD?
justification: Page 633: Below 30 feet RA at take-off when a LOCalizer (LOC) signal is available and during landing, the roll bar is replaced by a yaw bar index.

question: Which aircraft system uses the Aircraft Communication Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) function to exchange flight plan data with the ground?
justification: Page 704: The FMS uses the Aircraft Communication Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) function to exchange data between the ground station and the master FMGC.

question: What is the purpose of the 'A/THR instinctive disconnect' switches on the thrust levers?

options.b: To manually disconnect the autothrust and adjust thrust to the lever position
options.c: To toggle between Speed and Mach modes

justification: Page 635 & 676: A/THR is manually disconnected: - either by pressing the A/THR instinctive disconnect switch... When the disconnection is made by the instinctive disconnect P/B, the thrust is immediately adjusted to the thrust lever position.

question: What is the maximum number of flight plan legs that can be downloaded into the MCDU for the 'BACK-UP NAV' function?
justification: Page 708: Downloading includes waypoint position... in a maximum of 150 legs.

question: What does a green dot on the PFD airspeed scale represent?

options.b: The engine out operating speed in clean configuration

justification: Page 670: GREEN DOT: This is the engine out operating speed in clean configuration. It is displayed in flight only by a green dot.

question: When the SPD/MACH control knob is pulled, what reference speed does the FMGC use?

options.a: A managed speed calculated by the FMGC
options.b: A selected reference speed displayed on the FCU

justification: Page 691: PULLED: When pulled, the Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC) uses a selected reference speed which is displayed on the FCU.

question: If an FCU knob is turned to change a speed but is not pulled within a specific time, what happens to the display?

options.a: The display is locked to the new value
options.b: The display reverts to dashes after 45 seconds
options.c: A 'CHECK FCU' warning appears on the EWD

justification: Page 691: TURNED: ... If the knob is not pulled within 45 seconds the display reverts to dashes.

question: What color is the 'GLIDE SLOPE' text on the PFD when the Landing System (LS) mode is active?
justification: Page 482: ILS information is displayed in magenta.

question: What is the primary source of GPS position data for ADIRU 1 and ADIRU 3 in normal operation?
justification: Page 486: In normal operation, the GPS 1 data are used by the Air Data/Inertial Reference Units (ADIRUs) 1 and 3.

question: If both FMGCs fail, what system can be used to optionally retrieve ADIRS parameters?
justification: Page 681: NOTE: In case of loss of both FMGC, the ADIRS parameters can be optionally retrieved using the back-up nav on the MCDU.

question: What is the definition of the Cost Index (CI) used in the FM performance function?

options.a: The ratio of takeoff weight to fuel density
options.b: The ratio of cost of time to the cost of fuel
options.c: The total landing fee divided by distance flown

justification: Page 705: A CI is defined as the ratio of cost of time to the cost of fuel.

question: In the MCDU 'POSITION MONITOR' page, which position source is indicated by 'GPIRS'?

options.b: A hybrid mix of GPS and IRS data

justification: Page 486: The Inertial Reference (IR) portion... gives to the FMGC... hybrid GPIR data. Page 381 shows the GPIRS line on the MCDU.

question: If AP 1 is active and disengages, what is the behavior of the standby AP 2 in a dual-channel approach?

options.a: The flight enters manual law immediately
options.b: A switching is done to the AP 2 commands
options.c: The aircraft enters an emergency descent automatically

justification: Page 683: A switching is done to the AP 2 commands in case of AP1 disengagement.

question: Which cockpit indication confirms the engagement of the A/THR function?

options.a: The A/THR P/BSW on the FCU is lit
options.b: Thrust levers move to the CL detent automatically
options.c: A green 'A/THR' message on the Engine/Warning Display

justification: Page 635: When A/THR is engaged: - the FCU A/THR P/BSW is lit.

question: When the FCU Heading/Track lateral control knob is pushed, what is the status of the navigation mode?
justification: Page 693: PUSHED: When pushed, the navigation mode is armed.

question: During 'INDEPENDENT MODE' operation, what happens if an entry is made on MCDU 1?

options.a: The entry is automatically synchronized to FMGC 2
options.b: The entry is not applied to the other MCDU
options.c: The system triggers an FMS DISAGREE Master Caution

justification: Page 702: In independent mode, both MCDUs operate separately. Although the cross talk is present, an entry on one MCDU is not applied to the other one.

question: Which MCDU page is used to activate the 'BACK-UP NAV' function if both FM parts fail?
justification: Page 708: The MCDU B/UP NAV is activated through the 'SELECT NAV B/UP” prompt on the MCDU MENU page.

question: When 'BACK-UP NAV' is active, what color and line style is used to display the flight plan on the ND?
justification: Page 708: In all cases, the flight plan line is dashed in green (as NAV mode cannot be engaged).

question: What event will automatically deactivate 'Backup Navigation' and return control to the FM?

options.b: The onside FM becomes healthy while the offside FM is failed
options.c: Selection of 'PLAN' mode on the EFIS control panel

justification: Page 709: Backup Navigation is deactivated upon one of the following events: ... - The following condition becomes true: onside FM is Healthy and offside FM is failed.

question: During which phase of landing are the three green bars of the FD pushbuttons automatically illuminated?
justification: Page 631: Upon FCU power up... or when losing the AP during the roll out phase of the landing, the three green bars of the FD P/BSWs come on automatically.

question: Which button on the FCU allows the selection of Metric Altitude display on the ECAM?
justification: Page 695: This METRIC ALT P/BSW is used to display the FCU altitude target in meter in the lower part of the lower ECAM display unit.

question: Under what Ra altitude is the 'alpha-floor' protection inhibited during flight (except immediately after liftoff)?
justification: Page 635: or in flight, when the alpha-floor is detected; this is inhibited below 100 feet RA except during the 15 seconds following the lift-off.

question: What does the symbol 'FPV' represent on the PFD?
justification: Page 631: There are two types of symbols: ... Flight Path Director (FPD) and Flight Path Vector (FPV) symbols.

question: Which unit calculates the aircraft's current track and FPA displayed as the FPV symbol?
justification: Page 633: The FPV symbol position is computed by the Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS).

question: What is the result on the flight control laws if the pilot moves the side stick while the Autopilot is active?

options.b: The autopilot disengages and the system returns to manual flight
options.c: The autopilot stays engaged but ignores the pilot's input

justification: Page 614: If the pilot moves the side stick when the AFS is active, it disengages the autopilot. Back to manual flight...

question: How many pre-programmed cabin layouts can the Cabin Assignment Module (CAM) contain?
justification: Page 261: The CAM can contain up to three pre-programmed cabin layouts and 3 additional modified layouts.

question: What action on the FCU sets the 'managed' speed mode?
justification: Page 691: PUSHED: When pushed, dashes are displayed... The FMGC uses a managed reference speed.

question: What is the physical indication to the crew that a Radio Management Panel (RMP) has failed?

options.a: A red 'FAIL' light on the master caution panel
options.b: The blanking of the display windows on the RMP
options.c: A steady 'COM FAIL' message on the ND

justification: Page 76: A RMP failure is indicated by the blanking of the display windows.

question: When a failed RMP is selected 'OFF', what action does it take to assist the rest of the system?

options.b: It sends a discrete signal for system reconfiguration
options.c: It forces the remaining RMPs into 'NAV' mode

justification: Page 76: When selected off, the RMP sends a discrete signal for system reconfiguration.

question: Which SATCOM component is described as the 'heart' of the system, handling protocol and modulation?
justification: Page 104: SDU: The SDU is the heart of the SATCOM system. It does most of the data-handling, protocol, modulation/coding...

question: Where is the SATCOM Satellite Data Unit (SDU) installed?
justification: Page 71: The SDU is installed in the aft avionics rack 80VU.

question: What are the two possible power supply configurations for the SATCOM Intermediate Gain Antenna (IGA)?

question: What are the four essential parameters required for the initialization of the ATSU router?

question: Which panel allows the crew to select radio frequencies and courses in case both FMGCs fail?

options.b: Measurement of the time delay of reply pulses

options.b: The other FMGC (FMGC 2) tunes it directly or through its RMP

options.b: The aural message is 'TERRAIN' only and is not followed by 'PULL UP'

options.c: ADIRU ground speed and Glide Slope status
